items: It is a highly challenging problem and remains open, especially when no extra information (e.g., depth, lidar and/or multi-frames) can be leveraged in training and/or inference.
The proposed MonoCon method does not use any extra information and seeks a minimally-simple design with very promising performance and real-time inference speed achieved.
The SMOKE method (Liu, Wu, and Tóth 2020) does not learn any 2D task.
In exploiting 2D-3D geometric constraints, existing work compute 3D locations explicitly based on 2D predictions, and thus often suffer from the well-known error amplification effect.
